QUESTION:
What is the recommended dose of Levothyroxine Sodium for pediatric patients?

RESPONSE:
The recommended starting daily dosage of levothyroxine sodium for pediatric patients with hypothyroidism is based on body weight and age: 0 to 3 months: 10 to 15 mcg/kg/day; 3 to 6 months: 8 to 10 mcg/kg/day; 6 to 12 months: 6 to 8 mcg/kg/day; 1 to 5 years: 5 to 6 mcg/kg/day; 6 to 12 years: 4 to 5 mcg/kg/day; greater than 12 years but growth and puberty incomplete: 2 to 3 mcg/kg/day; and when growth and puberty are complete: 1.6 mcg/kg/day. The dosage should be titrated every 2 weeks based on serum TSH or free-T4 levels until the patient is euthyroid. Dosage adjustments should be made based on clinical response and laboratory parameters. For pediatric patients from birth to 3 months at risk for cardiac failure, start with a lower dosage and increase every 4 to 6 weeks. For those at risk for hyperactivity, start at one-fourth the recommended full replacement dosage and increase weekly by one-fourth until the full recommended replacement dosage is reached.
